---
title: "Results, Reports, and Diagrams"
subtitle: "How does verified evidence become a Python-facing presentation?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** accepted numerical Result/report mechanics remain `STABILIZED`.
Structured authoring, its identity integration, and certified diagrams are a
`CONVERGING` target with implementation alignment pending. Adaptive
presentation-theme semantics remain a separate `CONVERGING` candidate.

## Separate materialized values from analysis evidence

`Result` is the shared immutable, already-materialized value role.
`AnalysisResult` is the receipt-backed terminal subset and exposes immutable
`ResultIdentity(plan_sha256, request_sha256, attempt_sha256, result_sha256)`.
`DirectSolveResult`, `DiagonalRootResult`, `OptimizationResult`, and
`HBBatchResult` derive from it. Each HB batch contains one `HBCaseOutcome` for
every declared case. The outcome is a derived view of its parent receipt: a
success exposes matrices and states; a numerical failure exposes its stored
`HBCaseFailure`. `ExplanationResult`, `CircuitDiagramResult`, and
`ReportResult` remain derived values and do not fabricate operation receipts.

## Reconstruct typed Results in Python

Python verifies the receipt and manifest before constructing an
`AnalysisResult`. Scalars and axes become SCNSim-registry Pint Quantities;
matrix payloads become labeled NumPy arrays with ordered coordinate, mode,
frequency, unit, and load-state metadata. An Analysis Result retains request,
attempt, artifact, and runtime identity even when its chunks load lazily.

Direct matrix channels use `(coordinate, ())`. HB input and output channels use
flattened `(coordinate, mode)` pairs in coordinate-major/mode-minor order.
`MatrixView.input_channels` and `output_channels` expose those exact stored-axis
labels; presentation never infers a reshape or relabels a mode.

HB operating-point arrays use the separate structured axes
`(pump_mode, node_coordinate)`. Each pump-mode label is an ordered integer tuple
in request pump-axis order, and each node-coordinate label is the sealed
compiler identity recorded by `state_node_map`. These labels are evidence, not
new View selectors or Port aliases.

The Result catalog describes artifact meaning: role, dtype, shape, axes, units,
and channel order. HB links carry case-local `{case_id, id, path, sha256}`
references. The manifest instead seals the byte tree. A repeated local ID or
SHA-256 across cases is valid; only the complete receipt-bound reference has an
addressable role.

No Result unpickles arbitrary Python objects. Missing chunks, mismatched shape,
unit disagreement, forbidden non-finite values, or a real/imag manifest
mismatch fails verification instead of returning a partial typed object.

## Keep presentation downstream of execution

Matplotlib renders numerical `show()` surfaces. `magnitude="linear" | "db"`
changes only displayed S magnitude; source arrays remain unchanged. Every
theme entry accepts only `Theme.AUTO`, `Theme.LIGHT`, or `Theme.DARK` and
raises `TypeError` for raw strings. Matplotlib still returns a real `Figure`,
Schemdraw a real `Drawing`, and HTML presentation its HTML object.

`Theme.AUTO` uses a light-styled portable static fallback and a self-contained
SVG/HTML rich representation whose foreground and background switch together
under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`. `Theme.LIGHT` and `Theme.DARK` remain
fixed. Existing `Drawing.save()` and `Figure.savefig()` preserve an explicit
theme; `AUTO` saves the light fallback. Presentation does not read environment
variables or mutate global Matplotlib/Schemdraw configuration.

Notebook rich display wraps the same SVG in self-contained zoom, pan, copy,
reset, and open controls. If JavaScript or clipboard access is blocked,
ordinary scrolling and the static SVG remain readable. These controls do not
alter the returned object, its geometry, a report, or static output.

The light and dark palettes share one paired ten-color cycle. Changing theme
cannot change arrays, curve/case order, line count, labels, diagram geometry,
layout, topology, or Plan/request/Result identity.

| Role | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| background | `#ffffff` | `#111827` |
| foreground | `#243044` | `#eaf2fb` |
| secondary text | `#5b677a` | `#a8b7ca` |
| grid/border | `#d8e1ec` | `#2b3a4f` |
| primary accent | `#2f80d1` | `#7bb7f0` |

The paired line cycle, in order, is
`#2f80d1/#7bb7f0`, `#c76b00/#f2a65a`, `#2e7d32/#7dcc8a`,
`#7e57c2/#b39ddb`, `#c44536/#ff8a80`, `#0f766e/#2dd4bf`,
`#a16207/#facc15`, `#be185d/#f472b6`, `#0e7490/#22d3ee`, and
`#475569/#cbd5e1`. Each pair is the light/dark rendering of one trace index.

## Structured diagram implementation target

[Structured Circuit Authoring and Certified Diagrams](../contracts/automatic-semantic-circuit-diagram-layout.qmd)
is the sole `CONVERGING` semantic authority. It replaces the prior inferred
neighbor partition and pre-render catalog with explicit series, parallel,
branch, bus, tap, link, exposure, coupling, and recursive ownership facts.

Runtime alignment is pending. The design below records how an implementation
must preserve the contract; it does not describe completed behavior or
establish implementation conformance.

### Package and capture boundaries

Implementation remains separated behind private diagram boundaries:

| Boundary | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| snapshot and expected evidence | capture one immutable structured Plan; derive visible expectations and separate complete source rows |
| authoring IR | retain recursive scopes and explicit structured operators without intent inference |
| scene and local layout | expand native parts, pack child scenes, and emit one neutral scene |
| independent witnesses | reconstruct only visible electrical and ownership observations from the scene |
| frozen serialization | expose the checked scene through one immutable result |

Capture must be pure. Coordinate promotion and normalization operate on copied
records; the renderer cannot mutate a Plan temporarily and restore it. The
same capture feeds compiler preflight. The existing canonical encoder remains
the current implementation baseline. Target identity integration must
deliberately add the structural declarations rather than claiming compatibility
by similarity.

The expected-visible manifests derive independently from the structured source
snapshot or compiled expansion. Complete authored operator, exposure,
alias, parameter-definition, parameter-binding, effective-point, unit, bus,
tap, ground-provenance, and ownership records remain separate verified source
rows. Observed witnesses derive only from emitted neutral geometry and may not
read placement tables, source rows, or hidden answers.

### Compiled matrix-stamp projection

The compiled projection remains a complete **matrix-stamp** view, never a
scalar-equivalent circuit. With the existing `exp(-i omega t)` convention and
$s=-i\omega$, each series station contributes

$$
Y_{\mathrm{series}} =
B_s (R + sL)^{-1} B_s^{\mathsf T},
$$

and each terminal half-shunt contributes

$$
Y_{\mathrm{half\text{-}shunt}} =
B_t (G/2 + sC/2) B_t^{\mathsf T}.
$$

The expansion evidence rows already contain half-scaled shunt coefficients;
the renderer must not divide them again. Both half-shunt contributions remain
visible and auditable. Symmetric entries describe one reciprocal coefficient
relation, not duplicate physical couplings.

Native diagonal glyphs associate a matrix coefficient with its station and
conductor. They are not independent executable scalar branches. Off-diagonal
$R$ is not a galvanic resistor, and off-diagonal $L$ remains a signed,
oriented mutual term. The visible table/legend retains every coefficient,
sign, unit, incidence, section/end/station, conductor order, and exact zero.
The observed witness reconstructs these facts from the neutral scene instead
of copying the expected table.

### Structured native scene and local layout

Authoring IR mirrors the declared hierarchy and operators. It does not derive
S/P/M interfaces, a quotient topology, a global physical flow, or a second
electrical graph. Every inline Subsystem and reusable Composite expands its
native child diagram in a measured ownership region with a visible ID.

The renderer first measures native/operator blocks, complete independent
multi-terminal or Composite peers, and complete child regions. A parent then
packs those units without rewriting child internals and attaches connectors at
authored endpoints or public anchors. Buses and links remain conductive routing
demands rather than component slots or inferred pairwise relations. This also
supports scopes containing native peers but no child Subsystem.

Automatic layout uses local conventions for the authored operator:

- a single series defaults horizontal and retains electrical order;
- every parallel defaults to a vertical start-to-end path with branches
  left-to-right; a parallel-local horizontal hint rotates those paths without
  reversing pins or members, while a scope axis does not rotate them;
- branch members depart their declared bus/tap without severing it;
- bus taps share one net while retaining separate attachment sites;
- each N-link remains one zero-component conductive relation whose shared
  geometry is emitted once;
- intrinsic, parent-applied, and Port-local ground structures remain at their
  authored locality while resolving to one canonical reference; and
- mutual couplings remain nonconductive and oriented.

An optional `SchematicLayout` applies strict axes, complete local permutations,
terminal sides, Port sides, and named-tap order over live authored handles. The
tap mapping constrains only explicitly declared taps within the owning bus
segment; implicit direct-bus contacts remain automatic. No hint can introduce
topology, raw coordinates, current flow, or a new electrical order. Parent
layout treats each measured child scene as one packed unit and connects only
registered public anchors.

The current renderer revision retains the local `U = 2.2` setting, actual font
metrics, separate readable name/value boxes, registered anchors, obstacle
clearance, continuous same-net paths, true T junctions, and other-net jump
arcs. `U = 2.2` is an implementation setting, not a TARGET semantic threshold
or user Gate. The main authoring image uses conventional native symbols, wires,
junctions, Ports, local grounds, physical coupling marks, and subtle titled
ownership regions. Operator/debug marks, routing guides, and private aliases do
not appear in that image. Ownership regions and labels remain unmistakably
nonconductive. Literal authored local IDs remain literal display identities;
the renderer neither title-cases them nor invents compact aliases. The existing
`show_provenance=True` default emits a compact separated footer that can be
hidden without changing the circuit scene or evidence.

An authoring `NodeMark` may be unlabelled; required compiled-marker labels stay
visible. A connected two-ray bend or contact may harmlessly carry a filled dot,
and every true three-or-more-ray wire junction carries one. Isolated dots and
marks that imply a different-net connection are invalid, but the renderer does
not reject a dot merely because it has only two incident rays. Mutual winding
dots are separate marks whose orientation evidence remains visible.

Ordinary L/JJ glyphs in the normal schematic need neither direction arrows nor
`+`/`−` reference-polarity signs. Ordered model endpoints and branch reference
conventions remain intact through rotation without being claimed as visible
facts of an unmarked symmetric body. Mutual winding dots, their endpoint
incidence, and coupling information retain sufficient visible relative polarity.
A presentation of signed branch current, voltage, or phase must explain its
reference endpoints. This is a presentation responsibility, not a new
signed-result API or a claim that diagram rendering computes those quantities.

Layout is deterministic only for the same renderer revision, inputs, Theme,
font files, and metrics environment. The contract does not prescribe a global
graph-search algorithm or promise all graphs are layoutable. Failure reports
the affected declaration or constraints and returns no partial/best-effort
certified result.

### Independent witnesses and frozen output

Witness A reconstructs electrical bodies, terminals, wires, zero-wire
equivalence, grounds, Ports, couplings, and compiled matrix associations. It
checks authoring geometry against the exact Plan and point, or compiled geometry
against the exact compiler-emitted expansion for that Plan and point. This is
projection correspondence. With `show_parameter_values=True`, A also
reconstructs every displayed effective scalar physical value and displayed unit
and compares them with that same resolved point. Hidden value labels make no
visible-scalar-label claim, although the certificate still binds the exact
effective point. This qualification does not weaken the compiled projection's
matrix, coefficient, sign, unit, half-shunt, or omission evidence.

For unmarked ordinary symmetric two-terminal bodies, including L/JJ, A may
compare electrical evidence modulo endpoint-reference reversal. It does not
reconstruct an ordered endpoint pair from hidden placement, source rows, or
expected metadata, and missing polarity signs are not an audit failure.
Complete ordered model orientation remains separately verified source/provenance
evidence. For mutually coupled branches, A reconstructs relative polarity from
actual visible winding dots, their endpoint incidence, and coupling information;
a consistent reference reversal carries the corresponding coupling-sign
transformation, never deletion of sign evidence. Required oriented compiled
evidence remains unchanged.

With `show_parameter_values=True`, the mutual annotation exposes its signed
numerical coefficient. With values hidden, sign-only coupling information
(negative, positive, or zero) remains alongside visible dot/incidence evidence;
the hidden magnitude remains source-verified. A observes the sign in both modes
and the magnitude only when shown.

The witness is not an independent proof of numerical compiler lowering,
stamping, View/PTC realization, or solver correctness.

Witness B reconstructs visible child regions and headers, containment,
native-leaf and Port ownership, and cross-boundary electrical incidence. The
undrawn root envelope is scene bounds, not an observed ownership region. For a
single unlabelled child-boundary crossing, B checks visible wire incidence and
does not recover a hidden `PinRef` identity. It does not reconstruct invisible
operator IDs, link-call history, bus/tap names, or coordinate/branch/exposure
names. Internally, each B boundary record contains the visible region path,
parent, and literal local title; either an unlabelled-only boundary mode or its
visible named boundary; the electrical net; and the visible inside/outside
contact sets. It never stores a hidden exposure ID as an observed fact. Complete
aliases, parameter definitions and bindings, effective point, units, ground
provenance, and other authoring facts remain separately available as verified
source/provenance rows rather than being smuggled into scene metadata.
`audit.show()` labels observed A, observed B, visible-value checks, and captured
source/provenance as distinct evidence classes. Human review C alone decides
whether the Plan is the intended circuit.

Only after A/B agree is the neutral scene frozen. `CircuitDiagramResult.show()`
returns a real Schemdraw `Drawing` through a supported read-only facade. The
existing `Drawing.save()` remains the static API; there is no new save/export
method. Notebook controls and static fallback serialize the same scene.

The optional `presentation_sha256` excludes its own displayed annotation. It
is presentation identity, not an authenticity/security signature, and does
not alter Plan, compiler, request, Result, connectivity, semantic, or
expanded-graph identities.

### TARGET Tutorial alignment

The 16 canonical QMD Chapter containers and generated zero-output Notebooks
teach the target proposal through short model-first Lessons. Each Chapter is a
complete clean-kernel document; Lessons may share preceding state only inside
that Chapter. They are documentation artifacts, not runtime evidence:

- Chapters 1–3 repeat one complete fixed-value inline-resonator circuit, inspect
  its Plan projection, and only then ask Direct and retained-node questions.
- Chapter 4 defines independent inputs, binds them through registered physical
  fields, and inspects the Plan-specific consumers before selecting one point.
- Chapter 5 requests Cartesian and listed spaces, then inspects exact point
  outcomes and collects one already-computed typed quantity.
- Chapters 6–7 preserve the accepted optimization, report, and restart/resolve
  routes on the same physical model.
- Chapters 8–10 introduce Library and Composite only after the inline subsystem
  is familiar.
- Chapter 11 builds two inline LC scopes, compares automatic/hinted diagrams,
  and uses a separate complete Plan for a direct stitch.
- Chapter 12 teaches transmission-line context before complete matrix RLGC,
  compiled evidence, a tapped two-section feedline, and a selected whole-RLGC
  response point.
- Chapter 13 first assembles and reviews the complete
  parameter-bound feedline/readout/floating capstone before selecting probe
  PTC. Chapters
  14–16 repeat that complete model before independently selecting
  transformed/retained Views, HB, and Direct/HB requests.

Every ASCDLS diagram remains a projection of the explicit authored or compiled
Plan. It may bind one explicit `ParameterSet`, including an optimization
winner supplied by the caller; it rejects `ParameterSpace`. It does not create,
select, or depict a request-specific View, PTC-effective topology, or solver
Result. Exact point/audit identity belongs to the
[Parameter System Contract](../contracts/parameter-system.qmd#parameterized-diagrams).

TARGET Tutorial cells do not claim execution against the frozen runtime
baseline. Runtime implementation alignment, exact Human acceptance, and durable
stabilization tests remain later lifecycle steps.

## Assemble reports from explicit inputs

`ReportSpec.inputs` contains exact `AnalysisResult` objects already held by the
caller, and `ReportSpec.theme` selects the same strict presentation enum used
by diagrams and figures. Report assembly verifies result identities, preserves
each native grid, and records every failed outcome carried by an input HB
batch. Its HTML, tables, and embedded Direct/HB SVG use one theme; `AUTO`
adapts in the browser while explicit themes remain fixed. It does not search
the workspace, infer a latest Result, run an analysis, interpolate curves, or
decide whether a Design Target passed.

`ReportResult` is pure derived data, not a terminal operation. Its `save(path)`
accepts a new `.html` file beneath an existing parent, refuses overwrite,
writes atomically, and returns `Path`. The file is standalone and self-contained:
it embeds figures, summary tables, and complete source identities, but excludes
complete large raw arrays, workspace links, timestamps, and inferred PASS/FAIL.
Additional formats wait for a named consumer.

Suffix, missing-parent, and existing-target checks use `ValueError`,
`FileNotFoundError`, and `FileExistsError`; other filesystem failures retain
their ordinary `OSError` subtype. Export creates no operation receipt.
